# POL-NNN: {title}

**Status:** required | default | retired
**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD

<!-- A policy is a standing rule of conduct, not a decision (ADR) and not a
     description of the system (spec). `required` — must be followed; a
     violation is a defect. `default` — followed unless there is a stated
     justification to deviate.
     Policies bind agents and humans alike. Amending one requires explicit user
     endorsement. -->

## Statement

<!-- The rule, in one or two sentences. Imperative. A reader must be able to
     apply it without reading the rest of this document. -->

## Rationale

<!-- The failure this prevents. Where possible, the actual incident or class of
     mistake that motivated it — a rule with a remembered cause survives; a rule
     with only a principle behind it gets argued away. -->

## Scope

<!-- Where it applies and where it does not. Be explicit about the exclusions;
     an unbounded policy is either ignored or over-applied. -->

## Compliance

<!-- What following it looks like, concretely. A short do/don't pair beats a
     paragraph. -->

## Verification

<!-- How compliance is enforced or detected: hook, CI check, lint rule, review
     step, audit. If nothing enforces it, say so — an unenforced policy is a
     convention, and should be honest about it. -->

## References

<!-- ADRs, specs, slices, external sources. -->
